Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:10:1.english: He is negligent - And he does not have the [legal] status of one who stumbles.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:11:1.hebrew: דאתקיל - בדרך יבשה, ונתקל ביה בהמתו, והוי ליה איהו פושע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:11:1.english: Where he stumbled - On a dry road, and his animal stumbled on him, and he is [considered] negligent.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:13:1.hebrew: לזכות בחרסיה - שלא הפקירן, חייב. ובשאין מתכוין שוב לזכות בהן, פטור, דמפקיר נזקיו פטור:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:13:1.english: To acquire its shards - [Where] he did not declare them ownerless, [he is] liable. And where he does not intend to acquire them again, [he is] exempt, for one who declares his hazards ownerless is exempt.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:15:1.hebrew: והאיכא ר"מ דמחייב - מדקתני בברייתא "ולא סלקה ולא העמידה", מכלל דבהיזק דלאחר נפילה פליגי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:15:1.english: But isn't there Rabbi Meir, who deems [him] liable - Since the baraita teaches, "and he did not remove it and he did not stand it up," it follows by implication that they disagree regarding damage [that occurs] after the fall.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:16:1.hebrew: אף בשעת נפילה - ומשום דלישנא דברייתא לא משתמע בשעת נפילה, אצטריך לרבי אלעזר לאשמועינן דדייקינן לה ממתניתין דקתני תרתי, כדאמר אביי לעיל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:16:1.english: Even at the time of the fall - And because the wording of the baraita does not imply [at] the time of the fall, it was necessary for Rabbi Elazar to teach us that we infer it from the Mishnah, which teaches two [cases], as Abaye said above.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:1:1.english: Exempt according to human laws - As [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:1:2.english: And liable according to the laws of Heaven - Because he did not remove [the obstacle].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:2:1.english: By an atypical wind - For he is [a victim of] unavoidable accident.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי בתרתי פליגי - במתני' כשהזיק הכד בשעת נפילה, ופליגי כשהוזק בחרסי' לאחר נפילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:3:1.english: Rather, Abaye said: They disagree in two [matters] - In the Mishnah, when the jug caused damage at the time of the fall, and they disagree when [someone] was damaged by the shards after the fall.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:5:1.hebrew: במפקיר נזקיו - כגון זה, דמסתמא מפקיר לחרסיו. ור"מ סבר: מפקיר נזקיו חייב, דבור שחייבה עליו תורה — בבור ברה"ר, דהפקר הוא, חייבה. ור' יהודה דסבר פטור, [ס"ל] דהפקיר רשותו ולא הפקיר בורו — זהו בור האמור בתורה. ולקמן (בבא קמא דף מט:) פליגי ר' ישמעאל ור"ע בהא מילתא. וה"ק רבי יהודה: במתכוין לשוברה והזיק בנפילה — חייב; ובשאין מתכוין, אלא מתכוין להורידה מכתיפו ונתקל ונשברה — פטור, דנתקל לאו פושע הוא. ובהיזק דלאחר נפילה נמי, לקמן מפרש מאי מתכוין איכא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:5:1.english: With regard to one who renounces ownership of his hazardous property - Such as this [case], where he presumably renounces ownership of his shards. And Rabbi Meir holds [that] one who renounces ownership of his hazardous property is liable, because the pit for which the Torah held him liable — it was with a pit in the public domain, which is ownerless, [that the Torah] held him liable. And Rabbi Yehuda, who holds [that he is] exempt, [holds] that one who renounces ownership of his domain but does not renounce ownership of his pit — this is the pit stated in the Torah. And later (Bava Kamma 49b), Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva disagree on this matter. And this is what Rabbi Yehuda is saying: when he intends to break it and causes damage through the fall, he is liable; but when he does not intend [to break it], rather he intends to lower it from his shoulder and stumbles and it breaks, he is exempt, because one who stumbles is not negligent. And with regard to damage [occurring] after the fall as well, [the Gemara] later explains what "intends" there is.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:7:1.english: And since the Mishnah [deals] with two [cases], etc. - The Gemara raises this objection.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:8:1.hebrew: אלא בשעת נפילה - היכי איכא למימר נתקל פושע הוא? מה הוא יכול לעשות אם נתקלה בהמתו? דבשלמא נתקל הוא ונשברה כדו, איכא למימר איבעי ליה לעיוני ומיזל; אלא גמלו, מי איכא למימר הכי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:8:1.english: But at the time of the fall - How can it be said [that] one who stumbles is negligent? What can he do if his animal stumbled? For granted, [where] he stumbled and his jug broke, one can say he should have looked [where he was] going; but [regarding] his camel, can this be said?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:9:1.hebrew: שרעתא דנהרא - שגדל הנהר וכסה את עין הדרך, ופושע הוא בכך, שאילו היה הדרך מגולה, לא נתקל גמלו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:9:1.english: The inundation of a river - That the river swelled and covered the surface of the road, and he is negligent in [doing] this, for had the road been uncovered, his camel would not have stumbled.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 29a:9:2.english: Serata - [This is] an expression [related to] "extended [sarua] or stunted" (Leviticus 22).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:15:1.hebrew: אבל לאחר נפילה מאי - כי מפקיר נזקיו לאחר נפילת פשיעה מאי — דברי הכל פטור? הא איכא רבי מאיר דמחייב! ע"כ אפילו הפקיר, דאם לא הפקיר לא פטרי רבנן, דעליה רמי לסלוקי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:15:1.english: "But after the fall, what [is the law]?" - When he declares his damaging objects ownerless after a negligent fall, what [is the law] — [does] everyone [agree he is] exempt? But there is Rabbi Meir who holds [him] liable! Perforce, [this refers] even [to a case where] he declared [them] ownerless, for if he did not declare [them] ownerless, the Rabbis would not exempt [him], since it is incumbent upon him to remove [them].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:15:2.hebrew: אלא מאי ד"ה חייב הא איכא רבנן דפטרי - הו"מ לדחויי דלא פטרי רבנן אלא היכא דאנוס הוא, אבל לאחר נפילת פשיעה מחייבי; אבל היה קשה, דא"כ רבי יוחנן דאמר בסמוך "לאחר נפילה מחלוקת" לא הוה פליג במידי אדרבי אלעזר, ומתוך הלשון משמע שבא לחלוק על רבי אלעזר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:15:2.english: Rather, what [is the halakha? Does] everyone agree [that] he is liable? [But] aren’t there the Rabbis, who deem [him] exempt? - [The Gemara] could have deflected [this objection by saying] that the Rabbis only exempt where he was [the victim of] an unavoidable accident, whereas after a fall [due to] negligence they hold [him] liable; however, it would [still] be difficult, for if so, Rabbi Yochanan, who says shortly [hereafter], "After the fall is [a matter of] dispute," would not be disagreeing with Rabbi Elazar in any way, whereas from the wording it is implied that he comes to disagree with Rabbi Elazar.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:4:1.hebrew: פליגי בשעת נפילה בנתקל פושע - דלר"מ דפושע הוא — חייב. כל כמה דלא הוה ליה פנאי לסלק, קרי "שעת נפילה". ולאחר נפילה פליגי במפקיר נזקיו, ואפי' לאחר נפילת פשיעה, כגון ששיבר במתכוין; דרבנן דפטרי ס"ל דלא חייבה תורה אלא בור דאית ליה בעלים, כגון הפקיר רשותו ולא הפקיר בורו, או חפר בור סמוך לרה"ר. וכן משמע לישנא: "מר סבר מפקיר נזקיו חייב, ומ"ס מפקיר נזקיו פטור" — משמע דבכל מפקיר נזקיו פליגי, אפי' לאחר נפילת פשיעה. ועוד, דקאמר לקמן "מפקיר נזקיו מאי מתכוין איכא", האיכא לפרש במתכוין ושיבר כמו שפירש על שעת נפילה. ולא בעי לאוקמי אביי פלוגתייהו בלאחר נפילה בנתקל פושע — דלרבי מאיר דפושע הוא חייב, דהוי מפקיר נזקיו לאחר נפילת פשיעה, ולרבנן דלאו פושע הוא פטור, דהוי מפקיר נזקיו לאחר נפילת אונס, וכן אית ליה לר' יוחנן בסמוך — משום דמתני' מוכחא דבתרתי פליגי, ולא היה זה בתרתי אלא בחד, דחד טעמא הוא. והשתא נמי תרי "ומודים" דקתני בברייתא: חד קאי אשעת נפילה — דמודים חכמים לר"מ באבנו וסכינו ומשאו דנפלו ברוח מצויה שהוא חייב, אע"פ שלא היה לו פנאי לסלק; אבל ברוח שאין מצויה היה פטור, אע"ג דלא אפקריה, דסתם אבנו כו' לא מפקר להו כי נפלו שאין מתקלקלין בנפילתם, ומשום דלא היה לו פנאי לסלק מיפטר. דאי היה לו פנאי לסלק, הוה מחייב אפי' ברוח שאין מצויה, דכיון דלא אפקרינהו, עליה דידיה לסלוקינהו — כדאמר בסמוך דמתכוין לזכות בחרסין, ואפי' נתנו אחר שם, כדאמרינן בהפרה (לקמן בבא קמא דף מז: ושם): "בעל השור חייב בנזקי חצר, ובעל חצר חייב בנזקי הבור", ובשמעתין אמר גבי גלל דאם הפכה בפחות מג', אם נתכוין לזכות בה — חייב; אע"פ שהוא לא עשה בור זה, כיון דדידיה הוא, עליה דידיה רמי לסלקו. ואידך "מודים" קאי אפלוגתייהו דלאחר נפילה — ומודה רבי מאיר לחכמים במעלה קנקנין ונפלו ברוח שאין מצויה דפטור, אע"פ שהיה לו פנאי לסלק, דהוי מפקיר נזקיו לאחר נפילת אונס, ומצי אמר: "האי בירא לאו אנא כריתיה", כיון דבאונס נעשה. ולכך נקט קנקנין, שמשתברין בנפילתם וסתמא מפקר להו:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:4:1.english: They disagree at the time of the fall regarding whether one who stumbles is negligent - For according to Rabbi Meir, who [holds that] he is negligent, he is liable. As long as he did not have time to clear [it] away, [the Gemara] calls [it] "the time of the fall." And "after the fall" refers to their dispute regarding one who renounces ownership of his hazardous property — even after a negligent fall, such as where he broke [the jug] intentionally; for the Rabbis, who exempt [him], hold that the Torah only obligated [one for] a pit that has an owner, such as where he renounced ownership of his domain but did not renounce ownership of his pit, or he dug a pit adjacent to the public domain. And so does the wording imply: "One Sage holds that one who renounces ownership of his hazardous property is liable, and one Sage holds that one who renounces ownership of his hazardous property is exempt" — this implies that they disagree in all [cases of] one who renounces ownership of his hazardous property, even after a negligent fall. Furthermore, when [the Gemara] says later: "If he renounces ownership of his hazardous property, what [case of] 'intentionally' is there?" — [if it only applied to an unavoidable fall, why ask this, as] one can explain [it as referring to] where he broke [it] intentionally, just as it explained regarding the time of the fall! And Abaye did not want to establish their dispute as [being only] after the fall regarding whether one who stumbles is negligent — [meaning] that according to Rabbi Meir, who [holds] he is negligent, he is liable because it is a case of renouncing ownership of hazardous property after a negligent fall, whereas according to the Rabbis, who [hold] he is not negligent, he is exempt because it is a case of renouncing ownership of hazardous property after an unavoidable fall, as Rabbi Yochanan holds shortly below — because the Mishnah proves that they disagree on two [points], whereas this would not be on two [points] but rather on one, since it is one reason. And now as well, the two [instances of] "And they concede" that the Baraita teaches [fit well]: One refers to the time of the fall — that the Sages concede to Rabbi Meir regarding one's stone, knife, or load that fell in a typical wind, that he is liable even though he did not have time to clear [them] away; however, in an atypical wind he would be exempt even though he did not renounce ownership of them, for ordinarily one does not renounce ownership of his stone, etc., when they fall, since they are not damaged by their fall, and he is exempt [only] because he did not have time to clear [them] away. For if he had time to clear [them] away, he would be liable even in an atypical wind, since he did not renounce ownership of them, it is incumbent upon him to clear them away — just as [the Gemara] says shortly below regarding one who intends to take possession of the shards, and even if another person placed it there, as we say in [the chapter] HaParah (below, Bava Kamma 47b and there): "The owner of the ox is liable for the damage of the courtyard, and the owner of the courtyard is liable for the damage of the pit," and in our passage [the Gemara] says regarding dung that if he turned it over within three [handbreadths of the ground], if he intended to take possession of it, he is liable; even though he did not create this pit, since it is his, it is incumbent upon him to clear it away. And the other "concede" refers to their dispute regarding after the fall — and Rabbi Meir concedes to the Sages regarding one who brings pitchers [onto a roof] and they fell in an atypical wind, that he is exempt even though he had time to clear [them] away, because it is a case of renouncing ownership of hazardous property after an unavoidable fall, and he can say, "I did not dig this pit," since it happened through an unavoidable accident. And that is why it specifically mentions pitchers, because they break when they fall and ordinarily one renounces ownership of them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:6:1.hebrew: מדקתני תרתי - וא"ת, והיכי דייק אביי מדקתני תרתי דפליגי לאחר נפילת פשיעה? הא אפי' אי לא פליגי אלא בנתקל אי פושע הוא אי לא, איצטריך למיתני תרתי, שלא תאמר דוקא בשעת נפילה מחייב ר"מ, משום דנתקל פושע הוא והתקלה היתה שלו עדיין, אבל אחר נפילה שכבר הפקיר התקלה, פטר ר"מ, אע"ג דפושע הוא, כמאן דפטר בור ברשות הרבים. וי"ל: דאי לאו שרבי יהודה בא לחלוק עליו בזה, לא היה צריך להשמיענו, כיון דבהדיא תנן סתמא לקמן דבור ברשות הרבים חייב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:6:1.english: From [the fact] that [the Mishnah] teaches two [cases] - And if you ask: How does Abaye infer from [the fact] that it teaches two [cases] that they disagree regarding [damage occurring] after a negligent fall? Even if they only disagree regarding one who stumbles — whether he is considered negligent or not — it would [still] be necessary to teach two [cases], so that you should not say [that] Rabbi Meir holds [him] liable specifically at the time of the fall, because one who stumbles is considered negligent and the obstacle was still his, but after the fall, when he has already declared the obstacle ownerless, Rabbi Meir exempts [him] — even though he is negligent — like the one who exempts [one who digs] a pit in the public domain. And one can answer: Were it not that Rabbi Yehudah comes to disagree with him on this [point], it would not have been necessary to teach us [this], since we explicitly learn an unattributed Mishnah later on that [one who digs] a pit in the public domain is liable:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:6:2.hebrew: הוחלק אחד במים בשעת נפילה או שלקה בחרסי' אחר הנפילה - ה"ה דמ"ל איפכא, אלא דנקט הכי משום דסתם חרסים מפקיר להו, כדמוכח ההיא דקנקנים, ומים לא מפקר להו כולי האי; ועוד, דרב אוקי למים דמתניתין בדלא אפקרינהו. וכי פליגי בדלא אפקרינהו, דוקא בשעת נפילה פליגי, דלאחר נפילה מודה ר"י שעליו לסלק, כיון שהם שלו ויש לו פנאי לסלק. אבל בפלוגתא דלאחר נפילה במפקיר נזקיו, לאו דוקא לאחר נפילה, אלא אף לאחר נפילה שהיה לו פנאי לסלק פוטר ר"י, משום דהוי בור דלית ליה בעלים; ור"מ מחייב אף בשעת נפילה, כיון דסבר דנתקל פושע הוא ומפקיר נזקיו חייב:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:6:2.english: "[Another person] slipped in the water at the time of [the] fall, or was injured by the shards after the fall" - The same applies that [the Gemara] could have stated [it] the opposite way, but it chose [to phrase it] this way because ordinarily one renounces ownership of shards, as is proven by that [case] of the jugs, whereas one does not renounce ownership of water to that extent; and furthermore, because Rav established [the case of] the water in our Mishnah as [a case] where he did not renounce ownership of it. And when they disagree in [a case] where he did not renounce ownership of them, they disagree specifically at the time of the fall, for after the fall Rabbi Yehudah concedes that it is incumbent upon him to remove [them], since they are his and he has the opportunity to remove [them]. However, in the dispute regarding after the fall in [the case of] one who renounces ownership of his hazardous items, [it does] not [mean] specifically [immediately] after the fall, rather even after the fall when he had the opportunity to remove [them], Rabbi Yehudah exempts [him], because it is a pit that has no owner; and Rabbi Meir holds [him] liable even at the time of the fall, since he holds that one who stumbles is negligent and that one who renounces ownership of his hazardous items is liable.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:7:1.hebrew: מדמתני' בתרתי, ברייתא נמי בתרתי - וא"ת: מברייתא נמי יש להוכיח דבתרתי פליגי, דמדקתני "ולא סלקה ולא העמידה", משמע דלאחר נפילה פליגי; ועוד, דאי לא פליגי אלא בשעת נפילה, אמאי חייב בדיני שמים לרבנן דאית להו נתקל אנוס הוא? ובשעת נפילה נמי פליגי, מדנקט "מודים חכמים באבנו סכינו ומשאו", דלא מצי קאי אלא אשעת נפילה; דאי לא פליגי אלא לאחר נפילה במפקיר נזקיו, א"כ אפי' נוקי בהפקיר אבנו סכינו ומשאו לא יתיישב — דאי מודים ברוח מצויה דחייב, ושאין מצויה דפטור, א"כ לא פליגי כלל. וי"ל, דמברייתא לא מצי למידק כלל, דאיכא למימר דפליגי בשעת נפילה ולאחר נפילה ובחד טעמא, כדפרישית לעיל. והא דנקט בהאי "מודים אבנו כו'" ובהאי "מודים קנקנים", אורחא דמילתא נקט: דאין אדם מקפיד באבנו אם תפול ברוח מצויה, ובקנקנים כדי שלא ישברו מניחם בענין שלא יפלו ברוח מצויה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:7:1.english: Since [the dispute in] the Mishnah is with regard to two [situations], [the dispute in] the baraita is also with regard to two [situations] - And if you ask: From the baraita too one can prove that they disagree with regard to two [situations] — for since it teaches "and he did not remove it, and he did not stand it up," it implies that they disagree regarding after the fall; and furthermore, if they only disagree at the time of the fall, why is he liable under the laws of Heaven according to the Rabbis, who hold that one who stumbles is [a victim of] an unavoidable accident? And at the time of the fall they also disagree, from the fact that it states "the Sages concede regarding his stone, his knife, and his burden," which can only refer to the time of the fall; for if they only disagree regarding after the fall in [the case of] one who renounces ownership of his hazards, if so, even if we establish [the baraita] as [referring to] one who renounced ownership of his stone, his knife, and his burden, it will not be reconciled — for if they concede regarding a normal wind that he is liable, and [regarding a wind] that is not normal that he is exempt, if so, they do not disagree at all! And one can answer that from the baraita one cannot infer [this] at all, for it is possible to say that they disagree [both] at the time of the fall and after the fall, yet with a single reason, as I explained above. And that which it states in this [case] "they concede [regarding] his stone, etc." and in that [case] "they concede [regarding] jugs," it states the usual way of things: for a person is not particular about his stone if it falls in a normal wind, whereas with jugs, so that they will not break, he places them in a manner that they will not fall in a normal wind.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:8:1.hebrew: אלא גמלו בשלמא לאחר נפילה משכחת לה - דפליגי, כגון שהפקיר נבלתו אחר נפילתה בפשיעה, כגון שהוליכה במקום שיש לחוש שתפול; אלא בשעת נפילה היכי משכחת לה, דלפלגו כעין פלוגתא דפליגי בנתקל? וא"ת: ולוקי פלוגתייהו דשעת נפילה אכדו, ולאחר נפילה אגמלו, כדמוקי מתניתין: דהוחלק אחד במים — בשעת נפילה, או שלקה בחרסית — לאחר נפילה? וי"ל: חדא, משום דסתם חרסית מפקר להו, וסתם נבילה לא מפקר לה כחרסית. ועוד, מדקתני "ולא סלקה", משמע דכדו נמי היה לו פנאי לסלק; והואיל וכן הוא, אי מוקמינן לכדו בשעת נפילה, א"כ מיירי כדו בתרתי, ומדכדו בתרתי — גמלו נמי בתרתי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 29a:8:1.english: But [with regard to] his camel, granted, after the fall you find it - That they disagree, such as where he renounced ownership of its carcass after its fall through negligence — such as where he led it in a place where there is concern that it might fall. But at the time of the fall, how can you find it, such that they would disagree in a manner similar to the dispute in which they disagree regarding one who stumbles? And if you say: Let us establish their dispute of the time of the fall as [referring] to his jug, and [that of] after the fall as [referring] to his camel, just as [the Gemara] establishes the Mishnah — that "one slipped in the water" [refers to] at the time of the fall, or "was injured by the shards" [refers to] after the fall? One can answer: Firstly, because ordinarily one renounces ownership of shards, whereas ordinarily one does not renounce ownership of a carcass as [readily as] shards. And furthermore, since [the baraita] teaches "and he did not remove it," it implies that [with regard to] his jug too, he had time to remove [it]; and since this is so, if we establish his jug as [referring to] the time of the fall, then his jug deals with both [cases], and since his jug [deals] with both, his camel also [deals] with both:
